title: Tenali and the Precious Ring (मराठी)

full_text:
While enjoying an evening boat ride upon the Tungabhadra River, Queen Tirumala Devi leaned over the gilded railing to watch the lotus blossoms. Her ancestral emerald signet ring—a priceless gem engraved with the royal insignia of Vijayanagara—slipped from her finger and vanished into the swirling, deep currents!

Royal divers searched the riverbed for three days, but the rocky, murky bottom yielded nothing.
The Queen fell into deep sorrow, refusing to eat.
King Krishnadevaraya proclaimed a reward of one thousand gold coins to whoever could recover the ring.

Tenali Raman studied the river currents where the boat had been anchored.
He knew that predatory river fish, especially large catfish and carp, are attracted to shiny, glittering objects sinking through the water, often swallowing them whole.
He also knew that local fishermen cast their large drift-nets at that exact bend every dawn.

Tenali did not dive into the mud.
Instead, he took five hundred gold coins from his own savings and went to the main fish harbor at sunrise, just as thirty fishing smacks docked with their morning catch.

Tenali mounted a wooden crate and shouted in a booming voice:
'Listen, fishermen of Vijayanagara! By royal order, I purchase every single fish caught at the Golden Bend this morning!
Bring your baskets to my scale; I will pay double the market price in cash!'

The delighted fishermen brought forty baskets of fresh river fish to Tenali’s courtyard.
Tenali hired five trusted fishmongers, promising a silver coin for every belly cleaned, with one strict condition:
'Inspect the stomach of every fish with utmost care before washing!'

For three hours, the fishmongers cleaned the fish.
Suddenly, from the belly of a massive, thirty-pound river mahseer, a brilliant flash of green light illuminated the table!
The fishmonger cried out in amazement:
Inside the fish's stomach was Queen Tirumala Devi's emerald signet ring, completely undamaged and gleaming with peerless brilliance!

Tenali washed the ring in rosewater and carried it straight to the palace.
When the King and Queen saw the recovered heirloom, tears of joyous wonder filled their eyes!
The Queen rewarded Tenali with a diamond necklace, while the King distributed the forty baskets of cleaned fish to feed all the orphanages and hospitals of Vijayanagara.

The people celebrated Tenali’s brilliant deductive logic, marveling that while others looked into the mud, Tenali looked into the nets of nature.
moral: Careful inquiry and bold, unorthodox action recover what seemed irrevocably lost to the depths. [MR]
